name: Jeroham
overview: Jeroham was a male member of the tribe of Dan, noted primarily as the father of Azarel. His identity is grounded in this familial connection, with no additional personal details or roles recorded in Scripture beyond this. The biblical record mentions him specifically in 1 Chronicles 27:22.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroham means 'he will be compassionate,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew proper name. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God. This name highlights a characteristic of compassion, which may reflect the qualities valued in his family or tribe.
familyAndRelationships: Jeroham is explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Dan and is recorded as the father of Azarel. These are the only family relationships Scripture notes concerning him, with no further familial ties mentioned beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroham's significance in the biblical narrative rests chiefly on his role as the father of Azarel, situating him within the genealogical and tribal framework of Israel. His mention in 1 Chronicles 27:22 places him within the broader context of Israel's tribal organization and leadership during the time chronicled. Though not a prominent figure in terms of direct actions or leadership, his inclusion preserves the lineage and tribal heritage important to God's covenant people.
